newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner disappoints, tumbles on H1 data.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner disappoints, tumbles on H1 data.

text.p: Shares in Anglo-Norwegian construction and engineering company Kvaerner ASA tumbled into negative territory on Tuesday after the group released ite first-half results.
At 1304 GMT Kvaerner stood 5.46 percent, or 25 crowns, down at 433 crowns. The stock was 10 crowns up when the results were announced.
"The figures were extremely bad and show a pre-tax margin for the first and second quarter of less than one percent," said an Oslo-based analyst.
The London-headquartered company posted pre-tax profits up 19 percent at 840 million crowns in the first half, with operating profits at 963 million crowns versus 558 million crowns.
The results fell well below expectations.
"The pre-tax figure includes 575 million crowns in sales gains in the two quarters, so Kvaerner's ordinary business earned around 250 million crowns on revenues of 33 billion.
"Most analysts will adjust their margin estimates down for 1998 and 1999, the estimates are too high. Revenues are okay, but Kvaerner is not yet able to earn good money," the analyst said.
